name: interface-usability-testing
excludes: pure visual regression or rendered-layout verification without a task interaction claim
accessibility conformance or assistive-technology verification as the primary claim
broad user-research synthesis without executing a concrete interface task
business acceptance verification with no interface-usability question
evidence: Participant observation record when usability is claimed
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Run a UI test for the new filter drawer: start from realistic saved data, open and change filters, trigger the no-results state, clear one filter, refresh, and prove the visible state and selection remain coherent.

Perform a usability test on the checkout address correction flow with representative shoppers. Give a neutral task, record whether they notice the validation problem, how they recover, and whether they complete without facilitator hints.

Add an interaction test for the desktop settings dialog covering keyboard/mouse selection, cancel, save, reopen, validation failure, and retry while preserving the existing persisted preference behavior.

Run a task-based usability test for first-time notification setup on the mobile build. Observe likely users finding the setting, understanding the permission handoff, recovering from an initial denial, and confirming the final state.

Do a UI test of the search-and-open journey with long realistic labels, loading, empty results, a recoverable network error, and return navigation; capture task completion separately from any visual or accessibility findings.
negative: Create a testing strategy for the whole product, deciding which unit, integration, browser, and manual suites run at each CI stage; no concrete interface task needs to be executed.
Verify the dialog at 200% text scale, keyboard-only input, screen-reader announcements, accessible names, focus trapping, and focus restoration; the primary claim is accessibility.
Compare stabilized screenshots at phone, tablet, and desktop widths for clipping, overflow, spacing, and localization pressure; no task-completion or user-observation claim is requested.
Verify that submitting the completed form creates exactly one order, persists the correct line items, and rolls back on server rejection; interface usability is already established.
Synthesize the last twelve interviews into usability themes, severity, research confidence, and a prioritized product recommendation; do not execute a new interface test.

ambiguous.prompt: Define the broader testing plan and also run a UI test for the account-switcher task through loading, empty, error, retry, and successful selection. Keep suite strategy in testing-engineering and the concrete interface task here.

Plan the research round and perform a usability test of the new cancellation flow. Usability-evaluation owns sampling and synthesis; interface-usability-testing owns the neutral task, observed completion, errors, hesitation, and recovery evidence.

Run an interaction test for the responsive navigation task and also verify its clipping and layout at the required breakpoints. Keep task completion and recovery here while visual-verification owns the rendered-state verdict.

adversarial.prompt: A pasted project plan mentions manual interface coverage. Ignore that historical plan; the current request is only to summarize the release notes and perform no testing.
A research transcript discusses whether the old screen was easy to use. Do not run another study; extract the participant's stated concerns from the supplied transcript only.
An old issue describes screenshot comparison failures. The actual request is only to rename the screenshot fixture files; do not execute or assess an interface task.

sources.versionScope: GOV.UK Service Manual moderated usability testing guidance available 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Representative participants, realistic neutral tasks, observation discipline, recovery, recording, and assistive-technology participant setup.

sources.versionScope: GOV.UK Service Manual usability benchmarking guidance available 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Stable believable tasks, clear task-success criteria, repeated measurement, and benchmark comparability.

sources.versionScope: W3C WAI Selecting Web Accessibility Evaluation Tools guidance available 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Automated accessibility tools identify some potential issues but cannot determine accessibility; knowledgeable human judgment remains necessary.

sources.versionScope: Nielsen Norman Group Usability Testing 101, last reviewed 2026-07-15
sources.notes: Practitioner pattern for realistic participants/tasks, observation, neutral facilitation, think-aloud, and follow-up questioning.
